title: TensorPlate Roadmap Target
description: A future target that is not exact enough to be a platform support row: the SKU, machine shape, or validation environment is not yet named. Deliberately smaller than the support-row schema and NOT interchangeable with it — a roadmap target has no row_id, no support_level, no model_class_rows, no gate semantics, and no evidence, is never matched by `doctor`, and never counts as a supported or Planned combination. Promoting a target creates a new exact support row with its own fixtures and evidence; it never mutates the descriptor into a row. This schema versions independently of the cross-process protocol; consumers reject other schema_version values as static-config errors. Free-text fields must also carry a non-whitespace character; that rule is enforced by consumers rather than by a `pattern`, because regex dialects disagree about which code points count as whitespace (U+FEFF and U+3000 among them) and a cross-language contract must not depend on that.

target_id.description: Stable identifier, unique across the catalog and disjoint from platform row identifiers.

intended_release.description: Release line the target is aimed at, as prose (e.g. a follow-up line rather than a committed version).

target.description: What the target is, in prose. Deliberately not decomposed into accelerator/CPU/OS fields: a target precise enough to decompose is precise enough to be a support row.

blocking_dependency.description: What must exist before this target could become an exact support row.
